hand_value: LAND TRUSTS FOR WOMEN is an effort to give women control over their own destinies. Two groups of women have researched the concept of land trusts, and formed groups to acquire land for all women and children at all times. This would promote the spiritual, emotional, physical, cultural, and economic well-being of women, and preserve the land. Many of us love nature deeply, and need to live with green all around us and be self-sufficient. We feel caged in polluted, violent cities where we survive day to day by doing meaningless work or by standing in welfare lines. Financially poor women are unable to buy rural property. Private ownership creates hassles anyway. Putting land in a land trust removes it from the speculative market. It would be available to all women and children, whether they want to live there or just stop for a short time, camp out, and relax. We can help women set up local land trusts, or they can join us. Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon. Write OWLT, Box 1713, Eugene, OR, 97401, or California Women's Land Trust, c/o Carole & Yolanda, 1538 N. St. Andrews, Hollywood, CA, 90028.

Dear Ambitious Amazons: Thanks for the Land Directory and including us, it might be a problem, however, that our phone number was misprinted. Our real phone can be rung at (617)585-8826. We tried out the # as printed and it doesn't belong to anyone, fortunately. Anyway you could add that we'd like to hear from any of your readers who are seriously interested in biodynamic agriculture or conservation/ecology action. Furthermore, I'd like to point out again that we don't own Feathers Farm, at least not yet, and that even groups with more people and a deed are usually burdened, as we are, with immense ongoing financial pressures. I mention this because I have noticed recurring and unrealistic attitudes toward "wimmin on land" which range from idealizing our self-sufficiency to guilt-baiting out non-urban "privileges." Our desire to share the experience of the land is large and sincere (hospitality is central in our value system), but we are also thus more vulnerable to getting ripped off or imposed upon by bad attitudes. I applaud the Land Directory and your generous efforts in making it happen, hoping it is a big step toward valuable networking among the land groups themselves, as well as a way for us to reach out to travelling and urban lesbians. But it is important, in my opinion, for the "sisterhood" and the very survival of land groups to discuss and understand what can and often does go wrong, why groups don't make it, how to build a political analysis beyond our interactions with each other, the land and sexual identities. Let us not get too smug about "3000 acres of women-owned land" - we could fr'instance do another questionnaire to find out just what are all these wimmin doing on land, how many of us are actually secure in a modest financial sense? How might urban wimmin find appropriate ways to fit into our constant reality and vice versa? --Thanks, Peggy Gallagher, Feathers Farm, Box 19, Bryantville, MA 02327 (617)585-8826
